newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Turkish Cypriot speaks against Cyprus missile deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriot speaks against Cyprus missile deal.

text.p: A Turkish Cypriot representative urged U.N. envoys from Islamic countries on Wednesday to oppose Cyprus' plan to buy ground-to-air missiles from Russia.
The issue was raised during a closed-door meeting of the 54-member Islamic group at which views were exchanged on a number of issues, according to a participant.
Ambassador Nugroho Wisnumurti of Indonesia was also introduced as the group's new chairman.

Osman Ertug, representing the Turkish Cypriots, who have observer status with the Islamic group, was quoted as saying the deal signed last month with Russia for the purchase of S-300 missiles was "the latest step in a massive campaign of arms buildup and militarization by the Greek Cypriot side."
He said a defence pact with Athens also involved the construction in Cyprus of air force and naval bases for Greece and military spending of $2.5 million per day.
Turkey's deputy U.N. representative, Tuluy Tanc, was also said to have spoken in similar terms.
Turkish officials have threatened military action to block deployment of the missiles, which are not expected to be delivered until next year.

In a related development, Britain's special emissary for Cyprus, Sir David Hannay, on Wednesday completed a series of meetings with a large number of United Nations and other officials concerned with the Cyprus problem, including Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

The United Nations, the United States, Britain and other interested parties are trying to clear the way for face-to-face negotiations between the leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities by mid-1997.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops took control of the north of the island in response to a coup in Nicosia by the military junta then ruling Greece.
The United Nations has been trying for years to reunite Cyprus under a bicommunal, bizonal federal system.

The U.N. special representative for Cyprus, former South Korean Foreign Minister Han Sung-Joo, told a news conference in Nicosia on Wednesday after meetings with leaders of the two communities that "it would be somewhat premature to call for direct talks at this stage."
"We need more convergence of views to make such talks successful," he said.
